candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'In the year 500, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the life of Enoch. In that Parable I saw how a mighty quaking made the heaven of heavens to quake' — opening of the Noah-vision interlude embedded in the Parables. Tewahedo manuscript tradition preserves the Noah-vision as integral to the Parables (some Hellenistic-Jewish witnesses treat it as later interpolation; Ethiopian textual witnesses do not separate it). This editorial decision shapes how Tewahedo readers understand the Parables' coherence.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And on that day were two monsters parted, a female monster named Leviathan, to dwell in the abysses of the ocean over the fountains of the waters' — Leviathan as cosmic monster. Tewahedo iconographic tradition (preserved on some monastic church murals) retains Leviathan-Behemoth imagery as eschatological-feast preparation, paralleling 2 Bar 29:4, 4 Ezr 6:49-52, b. Sanh 99a — the righteous will eat of these monsters at the Messianic banquet.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'And the male is named Behemoth, who occupies with his breast a waste wilderness named Dūidāin, on the east of the garden where the elect and righteous dwell' — Behemoth and the Edenic geography. The garden-of-the-righteous remains east-of-Eden, preserving the prelapsarian topology that Tewahedo monastic spirituality maps onto sacred space (the church's qǝddǝst, holy of holies, symbolically corresponds to the inner garden where the righteous dwell).
